rounds.title: LOCKDOWN
rounds.narration:
At 8:15 PM, Victor Ross is found dead in the laundry room during a prison lockdown.
Security footage shows Victor entering the laundry room at 8:02 PM.
Two minutes later, a second figure is seen entering the hallway leading toward the laundry room. The image is too blurry to identify the person.
Victor does not appear frightened.
Investigators believe he was expecting to meet someone.

clues.text: Travis seemed distracted all day. He kept checking the clock during his shift.
I saw Mason near the laundry hallway before lockdown, even though he wasn't assigned there.
Derek stopped by the laundry area twice that day, even though his assignment was in another wing.

rounds.title: The Door
rounds.narration:
Investigators discover the laundry room door had been jammed open with a folded piece of cardboard.
The door normally locks automatically when it closes.
The cardboard appears to have been placed there hours before Victor's death.
This means someone may have planned access to the room long before the murder occurred.

clues.text: Mason was unaccounted for during part of the lockdown.
Travis knew Victor's work schedule better than anyone.
Derek and Victor had an argument earlier this week.

rounds.title: The Cardboard
rounds.narration:
Investigators searching the prison laundry area discover that the piece of cardboard used to jam the door appears to have been torn from a larger box used in the laundry department.
The cardboard isn't unique enough to identify who used it.
However, it confirms the person responsible likely had access to the laundry area before the murder.

clues.text: Travis asked to switch part of his work assignment the day before the murder.
Mason stayed near the laundry hallway after count even though his shift responsibilities were finished there.
Derek seemed unusually interested in what Victor was telling other inmates.

rounds.title: The Interview
rounds.narration:
Investigators interview several inmates who were in nearby cellblocks during the lockdown.
Most report hearing nothing unusual.
However, one inmate remembers seeing an officer speaking with Victor right before lockdown near the recreation yard.
The inmate is confident it was one of the two officers, but cannot remember which one.

clues.text: A few days before the murder, I caught Mason searching through incident reports that had nothing to do with his assigned housing unit.
I saw Travis carrying a piece of cardboard during his shift that day.
Derek seemed more interested than usual in where Victor was spending his time.

rounds.title: The Table
rounds.narration:
Investigators go back over the laundry room where Victor's body was found.
Next to the body, under a folding table, they find a piece of folded-up cardboard.
It had been wedged under one of the table's legs to keep it balanced.
There is dried blood on it.

clues.text: Travis keeps checking the clock because he's waiting on his court report. Or that's what he wants you to think.
Mason's been asking questions about everyone since the day he got here. Maybe he's not just curious.
Another inmate saw Derek talking to Victor the day before. He said Victor was smiling, and Derek looked like he was barely holding it together.

rounds.title: The Cellmate
rounds.narration:
Investigators interview Victor's cellmate.
The cellmate says Victor had been writing in a small notebook for about a week.
Two nights before the murder, Victor told him he had "found something big."
Victor wouldn't say what it was, or who it was about.
The notebook has not been found.

clues.text: Mason asked me who brings packages into the laundry. Not visitors. Packages.
Travis switched his shift to be in that laundry room all afternoon. That wasn't an accident.
Derek's been asking inmates who owes who money.

rounds.title: The Missing Pages
rounds.narration:
Investigators search the laundry room one final time.
Hidden inside a laundry basket, they find pages torn from a notebook.
The handwriting is not Victor's.
The pages are covered in initials, dates, and amounts.
One set of initials appears more than any other: ODH.

clues.text: Travis was in that laundry room all afternoon. The cardboard, Victor's schedule, the shift change. Add it up.
Mason was missing during lockdown, lingered by the hallway, and read reports that weren't his. It all lines up.
Derek argued with Victor, asked around about him, and was all over that laundry area. Add it up.

Author calls needed:  Method — cause of death was never established in the drafts. Mason's absences — what was he actually doing (his own investigation? something else?). Victor's notebook — did it survive, and where is it? The ledger — what exactly was Derek tracking (debts, packages, both)?  Working shape (for the author to confirm or replace): The murderer was Officer Derek Hayes (ODH). He ran a ledger out of the laundry — debts and kickbacks, initialed ODH. Victor, who collected secrets, found it ("found something big") and was writing it in his notebook. Derek argued with him early in the week, then tore cardboard from a laundry box, jammed the laundry room door hours before lockdown, and waited. Victor arrived expecting a meeting — the footage shows he wasn't afraid. The hidden pages were Derek's ledger, which is why the handwriting wasn't Victor's. Travis's cardboard was under the table leg, never the door.
